data.body:
Change https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2651 pushed for review (commit acefb1c8525a).

## Mechanism chosen: top-level `run-name:`, and why

Confirmed against GitHub's workflow-syntax reference: `run-name` "can reference the `github`
and `inputs` contexts", with a documented `workflow_dispatch` example. That settles the open
question in the ticket — the change/patchset numbers ARE available at dispatch time, before any
checkout, so no post-checkout step is needed and no new plumbing is added. `run-name` sets the
run's `display_title`, which is exactly the TITLE column `gh run list` prints, so the fix lands
on the surface that produced the misreading.

Alternatives considered and rejected:

- Changing `head_sha` — not in our gift. GitHub derives it from the ref a `workflow_dispatch`
  is dispatched on; a run cannot restate it. (Ticket already said this; confirmed.)
- Dispatching the workflow from the patchset ref instead of `main` — would make `head_sha`
  truthful, but the dispatcher (gerrit-to-platform, in the Gerrit container) targets a branch,
  and Actions only runs workflow files that exist on a branch. Rejected: large blast radius on
  a gate that is currently correct, for a metadata problem.
- A job-summary / annotation naming the patchset — still requires opening the run, which is
  precisely the cost the ticket is trying to remove.

## The expression

```
run-name: "${{ inputs.GERRIT_CHANGE_NUMBER && format('change {0} patchset {1} (rev {2})', inputs.GERRIT_CHANGE_NUMBER, inputs.GERRIT_PATCHSET_NUMBER || '?', inputs.GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION || '?') || format('manual dispatch on {0} (no Gerrit patchset)', github.ref_name) }}"
```

- AC1 — a run titles itself `change 2626 patchset 1 (rev <sha>)`. The true patchset revision is
  included as well as the change/patchset pair, so the identity `head_sha` should have carried
  is present in the listing itself. It is placed last so terminal truncation eats it first.
- AC2 — built only from `GERRIT_CHANGE_NUMBER`, `GERRIT_PATCHSET_NUMBER` and
  `GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION`, all already declared and already sent by the hook. No input
  added, none made required. The `||` fallbacks mean an input-less dispatch renders `?` rather
  than an empty/`null` fragment.
- AC3 — `tests/unit/test_gerrit_verify_run_name.py`, following the repo's existing
  YAML-parity precedent (`test_workflow_names.py`, `test_gerrit_verify_triage_comment.py`):
  `yaml.safe_load` the workflow, then assert on the parsed document — the run-name expression
  must reference both change and patchset inputs, must reference ONLY inputs the workflow
  declares (an undeclared one renders empty rather than erroring, which is the silent failure
  mode), and must have a `||` alternative free of `inputs.` references. Structural, not a
  string match on the file. Seen RED first for the right reason (no `run-name` key).
- AC4 — the non-Gerrit branch renders `manual dispatch on <ref> (no Gerrit patchset)`, so a
  branch-head/manual run is explicitly labelled as not a patchset run.

## Verification

`make lint` rc=0 (includes zizmor and actionlint over all workflows — actionlint type-checks
the expression, so the `format()`/`||` nesting is validated, not just the YAML), `make
typecheck` rc=0, mechanism ratchet `new=0 increased=0`, complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0`.
A new `tests/unit/test_*.py` is not a `test_helper` under the mechanism census (that kind is
`tests/_*.py`) and a top-level `run-name` is not a `ci_gate` (that shape is a step with `run:`),
so nothing new was added to the mechanism surface. Workflow re-parses with all 12 jobs intact.

No gate/vote behaviour touched, per the ticket's non-goals.

Not closing: awaiting `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` on 2651.
